rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says numerous reports attest to the great merit of the final verses of Sūrat al-Hashr.
rows.anchor: bu âyetlerin büyük faziletleri olduğuna dair müte‘addid rivayetler vardır

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: A report from Ma‘qil b. Yasār says that reciting the refuge formula three times in the morning and the final three verses brings 70,000 angels’ prayers until evening; dying that day means martyrdom, and the evening recitation has the same rank.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki: “Her kim sabahleyin üç kere

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Al-Deylemī reports from Ibn Abbas that Allah’s Greatest Name occurs in the final six verses of Sūrat al-Hashr.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan şöyle rivayet etmiştir: “Allah’ın İsm-i A‘zamı Sûre-i Haşr’ın âhirinde

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: In a report traced to Muhammad b. Hanefiyye, Ali tells al-Barāʾ to recite the first ten verses of al-Hadīd and the end of al-Hashr before invoking Allah by His Greatest Name, then give the quoted supplication.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali “yâ Berâ!” dedi, “Allah’a İsm-i A‘zam’ı ile dua etmek istersen Sûre-i Hadîd’in evvelinden on âyeti ve Sûre-i Haşr’in âhirini oku

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Al-Deylemī transmits from Ali and Ibn Mas‘ūd, as a prophetic report, that the passage beginning with “Law anzalnā” through the end of the sūra is a cure for headache.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den ve İbn Mes‘ûd’dan Resûlullah’a merfû‘an “لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا ilâ âhiri’s-sûre rukye-i sudâ‘dır” diye rivayet eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī reports a recitation tradition in which successive readers, through the Prophet, place a hand on the head when reaching “Law anzalnā.”
rows.anchor: çünkü ben Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den kıraat okudum, bu âyete geldiğimde elini, dedi, başına koy

rows.speaker: Cibrîl
rows.claim: In the same report, Gabriel tells the Prophet that the verse heals every illness except death.
rows.anchor: çünkü Cibrîl bana bu âyeti indirdiğinde elini, dedi, başına koy, çünkü bu her derdden şifâdır sâmdan başka ki sâm ölümdür

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: Citing al-Sarakhsī’s al-Mabsūṭ, Elmalılı recalls Ibn Mas‘ūd’s teaching that the Qur’an’s main purpose is acting on it, not mere recitation.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Mes‘ûd Hazretleri “Kur’ân’ın nüzûlünden asıl maksad mücerred kıraat değil, mûcebince ameldir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading these healing verses is not for incantation or musical display; one should reflect, gain knowledge and God-fearing, and prepare for tomorrow as 59:18 commands.
rows.anchor: segâhtan makam çatlatmak değil, elini başına koyarak düşünmek ve marifet ile bezenip haşyetullah ile dolarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming test before the Mighty and Wise God explains why Sūrat al-Hashr is followed by Sūrat al-Mumtaḥina, the test-taking sūra.
rows.anchor: Nitekim bu hikmete mebnî Sûre-i Haşr’i İmtihan Sûresi tâkip edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı closes by praying for forgiveness for believers and their predecessors, hearts free of rancor toward fellow believers, and increased faith and love, dignity, wisdom, and joy through mercy.
rows.anchor: gönüllerimizde mü’min kardeşlerimize karşı hiçbir gıll u gış bırakma, iman ve mahabbetimizi müzdâd, izzetinle i‘zâz, hikmetinle âbâd, rahmetinle dilşâd et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the pledge, the verse admonishes all believers, condenses the sūra and turns its ending back to its beginning; its warning against despair strengthens hope for the Hereafter and future.
rows.anchor: Bey‘attan sonra bütün mü’minlere bir nasihat olan bu âyet sûrenin hâsılını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı also sees the verse as an allusion to Sūrat al-Ṣaff’s theme of a firmly joined structure.
rows.anchor: aynı zamanda Sûre-i Saff’ın bünyân-ı mersus mazmûnuna bir ta‘biyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains “do not take as allies” as forbidding friendship, reliance on their protection, partisanship, admiration, or inclination toward them.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın gazab ettiği bir kavmi dost tanımayın onların velâyetlerine tutunmayın, taraftarlık etmeyin, bir şeylerine heves edip de meyl etmeyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common interpretation identifies the people God has angered as the Jews; the following sūra’s discussion of the Children of Israel fits this identification.
rows.anchor: “Allah’ın gazab etmiş olduğu kavim” tâbiri ekseriya Yahudîler hakkında vârid olduğu cihetle burada da murad onlar denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed referent is hypocrites who ally themselves with the Jews.
rows.anchor: onlarla müvâlâtta bulunan münafıklar veya sûrenin yukarısıyla münasebetine nazaran da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters suggest polytheists, especially the Quraysh polytheists, in light of the preceding sūra.
rows.anchor: müşrikler ve bâhusus Kureyş müşrikleri olması ihtimalleri de söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because qawman is indefinite, he concludes that the warning is not restricted to one known people but applies to any group characterized by the stated trait of despairing of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قَوْمًا nekre olarak îrad edilmiş bulunduğu cihetle bundan murad muayyen ve ma‘hud bir kavme münhasır olmayıp zikrolunan vasıf ile muttasıf herhangi bir kavme şâmil olmak gerektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The despair described in the clause is the defining trait that explains both God’s anger and the prohibition against alliance.
rows.anchor: Zira gazabın veya nehyin sebebi olmak üzere beyan buyurulan şu vasıf, onların vasf-ı mümeyyizleriyle bir târifi demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one grammatical reading, مِنْ is explanatory: the people in the graves are disbelievers, and the believers have despaired like those dead disbelievers.
rows.anchor: Birisinde ءَامَنُوا۟ beyâniye olarak kâfirleri beyan olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead disbelievers have seen their permanent place in Hell and their loss of the Hereafter’s blessings; with no hope of future gain or aid from the living, their despair is complete.
rows.anchor: kabre gitmiş olan kâfirler cehennemdeki ebedî mevkilerini görmüş, âhiret nimetlerinden mahrûmiyetleri tebeyyün etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the other reading, مِنْ is initial and attaches to “despaired”: the disbelievers despair of the people in the graves, meaning they have lost hope that the dead will be resurrected and live again.
rows.anchor: Öbürüsünde de ءَامَنُوا۟ ibtidâiye olarak yeise ta‘alluk eder, kâfirlerin ashâb-ı kubûrdan me’yus olmaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despair is itself disbelief and summons divine anger; he cites 12:87, which says only disbelievers despair of God’s relief, and warns against those who have given up hope in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı yeis bir küfürdür, gazab-ı ilâhîyi davet eder لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hopeless, like Iblīs, seize opportunities to do evil and drag those who assist them toward Hell through despair.
rows.anchor: Âhiretten ümidi kesmiş olan me’yuslar ise iblis gibi fırsat buldukça her fenalığı yapar, kendilerine yardaklık edenleri de yeis ile cehenneme sürüklerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He ends by praying that God protect believers from despair and make them rejoice in faith and hope for divine approval.
rows.anchor: Hak teâlâ kalblerimizi yeisten koruyup neş’e-i îmân ve ümmîd-i rıdvân ile zevkyâb buyursun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun “ٱلَّذِى” can be parsed as an apposition to the earlier relative pronoun or as an adjective of “ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفُورُ.”
rows.anchor: Bu ٱلَّذِى de baştaki ٱلَّذِى’den bedel, yahut ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفُورُ’dan sıfattır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He directs readers to 65:12, which also speaks of God creating seven heavens and their like from the earth.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Talâk’ın âhirinde geçen ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ وَمِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ [65/12] âyetine bak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the indefinite “seven heavens” uses indefiniteness to magnify the heavens as wondrous creation, echoing 6:102.
rows.anchor: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ [el-En‘âm 6/102] mazmûnu üzere semâvâtın bedî‘iyetine işaret olarak tefhıym için olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes seven as nonrestrictive, expressing multiplicity and spread: this is one seven among many heavens.
rows.anchor: İkincisi mefhûm-i adedle yediye hasr maksud olmayarak teksir ve intişar ifade etmesidir ki birçok semâların bir yedisi demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first reading here: the context concerns encompassing scope, and the definite numerical force of seven means the heavens must include all upper realms called heaven, not just the immediately visible planetary system.
rows.anchor: her hâlde evvelki vecih ta‘ayyün etmek lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the seven heavens as an expression of the whole cosmos knowable from Earth, noting that the verse’s repeated “do you see?” addresses human observation.
rows.anchor: bu âyetin مَا تَرٰى... هَلْ تَرٰى hitabları sarih demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Starting from a physical, Earth-based viewpoint, he treats Earth’s orbital sphere, including the Moon, as the first heaven.
rows.anchor: peyki olan Felek-i Kamer’i dahi dâhiline almış bulunan Felek-i Arz’ı birinci semâ saymak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercury and Venus orbit sunward of Earth, so he places them inside Earth’s first heaven rather than above it.
rows.anchor: Zühre ile Utârid’in birer felekte yüzmekle beraber merkez olan Şems cihetinde bulunarak mahrek-i Arz’ın içinde

rows.speaker: hey’etçiler
rows.claim: Astronomers who held Earth fixed and the Sun in motion counted the Moon first, Venus second, Mercury third, the Sun fourth, and Saturn seventh.
rows.anchor: Arz’ı sâbit merkez ve Şems’i seyyâre sayan hey’etçiler Kamer’i birinci, Zühre’yi ikinci, Utârid’i üçüncü, Şems’i dördüncü semâda sayarlar ve yedinci semâyı Zuhal’le tüketirlerdi

rows.speaker: eski Batlamyus hey’etçileri
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the old Ptolemaic astronomers imagined all seven heavens moving and attributed each planet’s motion to its carrying sphere.
rows.anchor: her seyyâreyi felekiyle hareket ediyor zannettiklerinden dolayı seyyârelerin hareketlerini bunlara atfederek bu yedi semânın yedisini de müteharrik addeylemişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against that model, he cites 21:33 and 36:40: celestial bodies are not fixed to turning spheres but each swims freely in its own orbit under the law of balance.
rows.anchor: وَكُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ [21/33; 36/40] mantûkundan gāfil bulunuyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats the spheres as boundaries, not moving tracks, and counts Earth as a planet; this shifts inner planets into the first heaven and adds the newly observed Uranus and Neptune.
rows.anchor: Biz o felekleri birer mahrek değil, birer muhaddid olarak mütalaa ettiğimiz gibi, muvâzene kanunuyla arzımızın dahi bir seyyâre olduğunu anlayarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His resulting order puts Mars in heaven two, Jupiter three, Saturn four, Uranus five, Neptune six, and the fixed stars beyond the solar system in heaven seven; Saturn is the gate of the fourth.
rows.anchor: O hâlde ondan ötede beşinci semâ, ahîren muttali‘olduğumuz Uranüs seyyâresi sahası, altıncı semâ da Neptün seyyâresi sahasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seventh heaven is the great realm of fixed stars beyond the solar system; the Milky Ways hint at many worlds, but people cannot distinguish their features or see farther than their aggregate extent.
rows.anchor: Bütün nazarlarımız mecmû‘u üzerinde dayanıp kalıyor. İşte cismânî nokta-i nazardan yedi semâ hakkında anlayabildiğimiz budur
